sentences.text: Ms. Shakti Tripathi - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/St Heard on I.A.No.30487/2024 which is third bail application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant Sabra Bano.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 366-A of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years and fine of Rs.2,000/-, under Section 376 (2)(n) of IPC and under Section 5(tha)/5 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000/-, under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life and fine of Rs.5,000/- , under Section 370(4)
of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years and fine of Rs.5,000/- and under Section 368 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years and fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulations.

Appellant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 21.11.2022 (I.A.No.12349 of 2022) and second application was also dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 19.07.2023 (I.A.No.9203 of 2023).
Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to evidence on record, submits that learned trial Court has erred in convicting and sentencing appellant.

It is also urged that there are material contradictions and omissions in prosecutrix statement recorded in the Court as well as her 2 CRA-4208-2022 statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C.
Initially, FIR was lodged against unknown persons.
There is no cogent evidence pertaining to appellant's involvement in the instant offence.

Further, after referring to deposition of prosecutrix's father and other evidence pertaining to age of prosecutrix, it is urged that from evidence on record, it is not established at all that on the date of incident, prosecutrix was minor.
Further, after referring to prosecutix's cross-examination, it is urged that it is a case of consensual relationship.
It is also urged that appellant has served substantive part of sentence.

On above grounds, it is urged that jail sentence of appellant be suspended and she be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.
Looking to overall facts and circumstances of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the sentence and release appellant on bail.

Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction to appear before the concerning trial court on 07.04.2025 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
3 CRA-4208-2022 C. c. as per rules.
